<comment datatype="string">Some non-enteric bacteria, such as the soil bacteria <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ORGANISM&object=TAX-354"><i>Azotobacter vinelandii</i></a>, <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ORGANISM&object=TAX-382"><i>Sinorhizobium meliloti</i> (previously known as <i>Rhizobium meliloti</i>)</a>, <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ORGANISM&object=TAX-304"><i>Pelomonas saccharophila</i> (previously known as <i>Pseudomonas saccharophila</i>)</a> and <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ORGANISM&object=TAX-294"><i>Pseudomonas fluorescens</i></a>, degrade D-galactose via the De Ley-Doudoroff pathway.  The initial reactions of this pathway convert D-galactose to D-galactonate, as shown in the pathway link to MetaCyc pathway <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=PATHWAY&object=GALDEG-PWY">D-galactose degradation II</a>.  In the pathway shown here, D-galactonate is further degraded to D-glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate and pyruvate by dehydration, phosphorylation, and aldol cleavage.
<p>
Direct utilization of D-galactonate via the pathway shown here has been shown to occur in nonpathogenic mycobacteria, <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ORGANISM&object=TAX-83333"><i>Escherichia coli</i> K-12</a>, and archaea [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/7287628">Szumilo81</a>, <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/211976">Cooper78</a>, <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/15474024">Lamble04</a>]. Nonpathogenic mycobacteria such as <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ORGANISM&object=ORG-5916"><i>Mycobacterium butyricum</i></a> grown on galactonate showed galactonate dehydratase, 2-dehydro 3-deoxygalactokinase (2-keto-3-deoxy-galactonate kinase), and 2-oxo-3-deoxygalactonate 6-phosphate aldolase (6-phospho-2-keto-3-deoxy-galactonate aldolase) activities in cell-free extracts [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/7287628">Szumilo81</a>].
<p>
D-galactonate can serve as the sole source of carbon and energy for <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ORGANISM&object=TAX-562"><i>Escherichia coli</i></a> [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/324806">Deacon77</a>].  The initial step in the degradation of D-galactonate is dehydration to 2-dehydro-3-deoxy-D-galactonate by <a href="/gene?orgid=META&id=GALACTONATE-DEHYDRATASE-MONOMER">D-galactonate dehydratase</a>.  Subsequent phosphorylation by <a href="/gene?orgid=META&id=DEHYDDEOXGALACTKIN-MONOMER">2-dehydro-3-deoxygalactonokinase</a> and aldol cleavage by <a href="/gene?orgid=META&id=DEHYDDEOXPHOSGALACT-ALDOL-MONOMER">2-dehydro-3-deoxy-6-phosphogalactonate aldolase</a> produce pyruvate and
D-glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate, which enter central metabolism.  Reviewed in Mandrand-Berthelot, M.-A., Condemine G., and Hugouvieux-Cotte-Pattat, N., EcoSal Module 3.4.2 [<a href="http://www.ecosal.org/">EcoSal</a>].</comment>

<comment datatype="string">2-dehydro-3-deoxygalactonate kinase catalyzes the second reaction in the degradation of D-galactonate, the
ATP-dependent phosphorylation of 2-dehydro-3-deoxygalactonate [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/324806">Deacon77</a>, <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/211976">Cooper78</a>].
<p>
Production of 2-dehydro-3-deoxygalactonate kinase is induced by growth on galactonate [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/324806">Deacon77</a>].  The
inducer is most likely D-galactonate itself, and expression is subject to catabolite repression [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/211976">Cooper78</a>].
<p>
DgoA: "<b>D</b>-<b>g</b>alact<b>o</b>nate" [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/211976">Cooper78</a>]</comment>

<comment datatype="string">D-galactonate dehydratase catalyzes the first step in the degradation of D-galactonate, the dehydration of
D-galactonate to form 2-dehydro-3-deoxygalactonate [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/324806">Deacon77</a>, <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/211976">Cooper78</a>].
<p>
D-galactonate dehydratase belongs to the mandelate racemase (MR) subgroup of the enolase superfamily
[<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/7855594">Babbitt95</a>, <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/15581566">Gerlt05</a>].  A reaction mechanism for the &beta;-elimination of OH<sup>-</sup> involving His185
as a general acid/base catalyst has been proposed and is supported by analysis of point mutants
[<a href="/META/reference.html?type=CITATION-REFERENCE&object=%5bWIECZOREK99%5d">Wieczorek99</a>].
<p>
Production of galactonate dehydratase is induced by growth on galactonate [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/324806">Deacon77</a>].  The inducer is most
likely D-galactonate itself, and expression is subject to catabolite repression [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/211976">Cooper78</a>].
<p>
DgoA: "<b>D</b>-<b>g</b>alact<b>o</b>nate" [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/211976">Cooper78</a>]</comment>

comment:
<comment datatype="string">2-oxo-3-deoxygalactonate 6-phosphate aldolase (KDPGal aldolase) catalyzes the final reaction in the degradation
of D-galactonate, an aldol cleavage resulting in GA3P and pyruvate which enter central metabolism
[<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/324806">Deacon77</a>, <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/211976">Cooper78</a>].
<p>
Crystal structures of KDPGal aldolase have been determined.  Comparison to the crystal structure of KDPG aldolase
led to the hypothesis that the V154 residue was involved in stereoselectivity of the enzyme.  A V154T mutant shows
reduced stereoselectivity, but also reduced catalytic efficiency [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/17981470">Walters08</a>].
<p>
Although KDPG aldolase (the <i>eda</i> gene product) and KDPGal aldolase (the <i>dgoA</i> gene product)
catalyze nearly identical reactions that differ only at a single stereocenter, they show only a low level of sequence
similarity [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/17981470">Walters08</a>].
<p>
Production of KDPGal aldolase is induced by growth on galactonate [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/324806">Deacon77</a>].  The inducer is most likely
D-galactonate itself, and expression is subject to catabolite repression [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/211976">Cooper78</a>].
<p>
DgoA: "<b>D</b>-<b>g</b>alact<b>o</b>nate" [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/211976">Cooper78</a>]</comment>
